pages.text: At sunset, Mila sits with Grandpa to hear a folktale from his childhood.
The story has a clever rabbit and a patient turtle on a long journey.
Grandpa explains that folktales often teach lessons about choices.
In one version, the rabbit shares food. In another place, he shares water.
Mila learns stories can travel and change small details over time.
Long ago, many families told stories aloud before books were common.
Now stories can live in books, audio, theater, and cartoons too.
Mila retells the tale in her own words to her little brother.
Her teacher says listening closely helps memory and language grow.
Mila smiles: every family story is a bridge from past to present.
